How Long Does AEO Take to Show Results? Realistic Timelines by Engine

How long AEO takes to work, from 2026 studies: first AI citations in days to weeks, steady visibility in about 3 months. Timelines by engine and 90-day milestones.

By Anupam Varshney, Founder, Octaloop

Short answer: A new page on an established site usually gets its first AI citation within days to a few weeks. Profound measured a median of 6.81 days, and other 2026 studies found 18 to 26 days. Steady visibility for your brand on the prompts buyers actually use takes longer: most published timelines point to roughly three months, and to three to six months before you can see the effect in traffic and pipeline. Google's AI surfaces and Perplexity tend to move first. ChatGPT is slower to start, but its citations tend to last once they arrive.

"How long does AEO actually take?" is the question founders ask right before they spend money on it (r/AISearchLab). Most answers online are one agency's estimate stated as fact. This guide puts the published timeline claims from 2025 and 2026 side by side, says who measured what, and explains why the engines move at different speeds. It then shows you when to keep going, when to change course, and what a realistic first 90 days looks like.

How long does AEO take, according to the published data?

There's no single industry benchmark yet. There are a handful of studies, each with a different sample and a different definition of "results." Here they are, with what each one measured.

Source (date) What was measured Timeline claim
Profound, Josh Blyskal (May 2026) About 900 newly published marketing pages, first citation in ChatGPT or Claude Median 6.81 days; 75% cited by 18.68 days; 90% by 37.10 days
Semrush (December 2025) 81 new FAQ-style pages on Semrush's own high-authority blog, tracked daily for 30 days Google AI Mode cited 29 pages (36%) within 24 hours, peaked at 48, and was down to 21 by day 30. ChatGPT search cited 8 pages on day one and 34 (42%) by day 30
Xpand Media, State of GEO 2026 (Q1 2026 data) 50 client engagements plus 200 control sites across five engines, January to March 2026 Median 18 days to first citation (25th percentile 8 days, 75th percentile 41 days); median citation half-life 91 days
LeadsNow (September 2026) 7,126 citation checks on its own domain, 19 May to 13 September 2026 Median 26 days for a new page to first appear; site-level rate took about three months to move from 0.4% to 51.3% on its easiest surface; 42% of pages hadn't appeared after 60 days
PromptCensus (October 2026) Weekly checks of 30 questions per industry in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, Japan, July to October 2026 Press releases that got cited took about a week and blog posts about two weeks. Only about 10% of press releases and 3% of blog posts were cited at all. ChatGPT barely cited the new articles
Goodie (June 2026) Agency's client experience (an estimate, not a controlled study) First mentions in weeks 1 to 2; consistent citations in 8 to 12 weeks; measurable business impact in 3 to 6 months; stable ROI after 6 months
Parse (May 2026, updated October 2026) Vendor guidance built on the Profound and Semrush data First citations in days to weeks; competitive position on revenue prompts in one to two quarters; training-data ("memory") answers on model release cycles

Read the table with three caveats:

  1. First citation is not the same as results. Profound's 6.81 days measures how long a new page takes to get cited once. It says nothing about whether your brand gets recommended for "best [category] tool," which is the outcome a founder actually wants. Parse makes the same point: the citation clock runs in days, but competitive position takes quarters.
  2. Survivorship hides the misses. The PromptCensus and LeadsNow numbers show that many pages are never cited at all. A median "time to citation" usually counts only the pages that made it.
  3. Most samples are established sites. Semrush ran its test on a blog with an Authority Score of 84 and said itself that these were "the best possible conditions." A seed-stage startup with a young domain should expect a longer flat start, as LeadsNow notes in its own caveats.

What about Octaloop's own numbers? We don't have a tracked timeline to publish yet, so we haven't put one in this table. We're logging time-to-citation for our own site and pages across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google, and we'll publish the results, misses included, once there's enough data to be useful.

Why do ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews move at different speeds?

Each engine gets its sources differently, so each one runs on its own clock. If you judge all of them on the same day, you'll draw the wrong conclusions. (For definitions of AEO, GEO and SEO and how they overlap, see AEO vs GEO vs SEO.)

Engine Where its answers come from What the timeline evidence says When to judge a new page
Google AI Overviews and AI Mode Google's own search index. Google says a page "must be indexed and eligible to be shown in Google Search with a snippet," with no extra requirements (Google Search Central) Fastest pickup in Semrush's test, but also the most volatile. Google notes crawling "can take anywhere from several days to several months" After indexing; watch the trend over weeks, not a single day
ChatGPT Live search for some prompts, plus what the model learned in training Slower to start but steadier: cited pages kept their citations in Semrush's test. Profound found ChatGPT used web search in 17.4% of 667,000 conversations overall, but in 53.5% of commercial ones (Blyskal research index, January 2026 data) Around day 21 to 37 for a new page; months for answers that come from memory
Perplexity Live web search on almost every query Usually described as the fastest. The 2026 data is mixed: PromptCensus found Perplexity took about twice as long as Gemini to cite new articles (10 vs 5 days for press releases) Within the first two to three weeks

Two practical points follow from this.

Buyer questions trigger live search more often. In Profound's data, commercial prompts sent ChatGPT to the web 53.5% of the time, against 18.7% for informational ones. Comparison pages, reviews and press coverage can therefore affect the prompts that matter for pipeline faster than they change ChatGPT's general knowledge about you.

The memory lane is slow. When ChatGPT answers from training data, new pages can't change the answer until a future model is trained on them. Parse estimates six to eighteen months for that lane. That's why fixing wrong facts ChatGPT states about your company can take far longer than earning a fresh citation.

Why do AEO results swing so much early on?

Because AI answers are not rankings. They're generated fresh each time, from a pool of sources that keeps changing. Every serious 2026 dataset shows the same thing:

  • Answers rarely repeat. In SparkToro and Gumshoe's study of 2,961 runs of the same prompts, ChatGPT and Google's AI gave the same brand list twice less than once in 100 runs, and the same order less than once in 1,000 (SparkToro, January 2026).
  • Citations churn month to month. Across 11.2 million citations from August 2025 to February 2026, 68% of queries that produced citations one month didn't produce them the next, and only 7% stayed cited for four months or more (Passionfruit, March 2026).
  • Brand presence decays fast after a peak. Across 857,000 daily reports covering 10,991 brands over ten months, the median brand's citation count halved 31 days after its peak, and the typical weekly swing was 51.8% (Trakkr, March 2026).
  • Mentions are steadier than citations. Over 12 weeks to 26 July 2026, the share of brand mentions changed 25% week to week, while the share of cited URLs changed 39% on ChatGPT and 41% on Gemini (BrightEdge, July 2026). If your brand keeps getting named, the fact that the cited page changes is normal.
  • Ramps aren't smooth. LeadsNow's site appeared in 2 of 488 checks in its first 13 days, then jumped to 31.4% on day 18. Its ChatGPT rate fell from 20% to 6.7% in 48 hours with no change to the site.

There's also a trap in the other direction: growth that isn't yours. In a natural experiment on one large site, ChatGPT referrals to pages that had been optimised grew 5.7x overall, but untouched pages on the same domain grew 3.5x anyway. The effect the authors could attribute to the optimisation was about 1.8x, and they called even that "suggestive, not conclusive" (Watanabe and Nakayashiki, arXiv, August 2026). AI search traffic is growing for everyone, so compare against a baseline, not against last quarter.

The practical rule: never judge AEO on a single check. Run a fixed set of prompts several times per engine, count how often you appear, and read the trend over 8 to 12 weeks. That's the same advice Goodie gives its clients, and it's the method behind Step 1 of our founder's playbook for getting your SaaS mentioned in ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews.

When should you keep going, and when should you change course?

The published thresholds give you checkpoints you can apply to your own prompt set.

Checkpoint Keep going if... Change course if... Basis
Days 0 to 21 Nothing shows up yet. That's the expected reading Your robots.txt or CDN blocks OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot or Googlebot, or the pages aren't indexed LeadsNow's flat start; OpenAI crawler docs; Google's indexing requirement
Around day 37 for a new page The page has been cited somewhere, even inconsistently A specific new page has no citations on any engine. Treat that as a prompt to check crawl access, indexing and whether the page answers the question clearly, not as proof of failure Profound: 90% of pages in its sample were cited by day 37. Parse notes that missing this mark doesn't by itself diagnose a problem
Day 60 for a page The page appears on some engines and some runs The page is crawlable and indexed but still uncited. Rewrite it or merge it; don't wait longer LeadsNow: of 25 pages still absent at day 60, one appeared later
Day 90 for the programme Your appearance rate on a fixed prompt set has risen, even with weekly swings It's flat across all engines on an unchanged prompt set. Re-scope the work before you renew LeadsNow's 90-day review; Goodie's 8-to-12-week trend rule
Months 3 to 6 AI referrals and "how did you hear about us" answers start showing up Citations exist but no buyer traffic. Check that you're winning commercial prompts, not just informational ones Goodie; Parse's one-to-two-quarter horizon

One rule of thumb runs through all of these: missing citations at day 30 is a waiting problem, but missing citations at day 90 is a strategy problem. If nothing has moved by then, publishing more of the same pages won't fix it. The gap is usually off-site: the engines don't see enough independent sources describing you.

What should the first 90 days of AEO look like?

Here's a milestone plan built from the evidence above. It's a plan, not a promise. Where you start (domain age, existing coverage, category competition) changes the pace.

Days 1 to 14: Set the baseline and remove blockers

  • Pick 20 to 30 buyer prompts with no brand names and fix the list. Adding prompts later makes your numbers incomparable.
  • Run each prompt several times on ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google, and record how often you're named and which sources are cited.
  • Confirm that AI crawlers can reach your site and that your key pages are indexed.
  • Write down your core company facts and fix anything the engines state wrongly (here's how).
  • Milestone: a dated baseline with an appearance rate per engine.

Days 15 to 45: Make your own pages easy to quote, and start earning mentions

  • Rewrite your most important pages with direct answers up top, comparison tables and dated facts. Goodie reports that restructuring existing pages shows results faster than publishing new ones.
  • Publish comparison and alternatives pages for prompts where competitors are named and you aren't.
  • Find the publications and roundups the engines already cite for your category and start pitching them. Our guide to digital PR for AEO covers how.
  • Milestone: first citations on long-tail and comparison prompts, on at least one engine.

Days 46 to 90: Build third-party proof and read the trend

  • Land placements, podcast appearances and review-site profiles. Use speaking slots and event recaps as extra sources. Our piece on events and conferences as an AEO lever shows how one talk becomes several citable pages.
  • Re-run the baseline every two to four weeks with the same prompts and the same number of runs.
  • At day 90, decide using the checkpoint table above: keep going, double down on what's being cited, or re-scope.
  • Milestone: a higher appearance rate on category prompts than at day 1, and you know which sources are driving it.

After 90 days the work shifts to maintenance. Citations decay (Xpand Media measured a median citation half-life of 91 days in its corpus), so refresh your most-cited pages and keep earning new coverage.

Can you speed AEO up?

Partly. You can't make an engine re-crawl or retrain on your schedule, but you can stop slowing it down:

  • Remove technical blockers on day one. OpenAI says sites must not block OAI-SearchBot to appear in ChatGPT search answers, and that robots.txt changes take about 24 hours to apply (OpenAI).
  • Improve pages that already get crawled before you write new ones.
  • Earn coverage on sites the engines already cite. A new page on your domain starts from zero. A mention in a publication the engine already trusts doesn't.
  • Publish consistently. Pages on domains the engines have cited before reached first citation faster in Xpand Media's corpus.

What won't speed it up: a single big launch followed by silence, buying a "guaranteed placement," or checking ChatGPT once a day and reacting to each answer. Google's own guidance on hiring an SEO now mentions "AEO" and "GEO" services by name. It tells you to ask "What kind of results do you expect to see, and in what timeframe?", to check that AI-search advice matches Google's official guidance, and it warns that no one can guarantee a #1 ranking on Google (Google Search Central).

Should you run AEO in-house or hire an agency?

A founder can do the first 14 days alone: build the prompt list, run the baseline, fix crawl access and clean up company facts. What's hard to sustain in-house is everything after that: checking the same prompts across several engines every few weeks, reading noisy data honestly, and earning the third-party coverage that turns early citations into lasting visibility.

If you're comparing agencies, ask three questions. Will they show you the appearance rate per engine on a fixed prompt set, with the number of runs? What do they expect by day 30, 60 and 90, and what will they change if it hasn't happened? And can they actually earn press and placements, or only publish on your blog? An agency that promises a timeline without showing its method is guessing.

FAQ

How long does AEO take to work?

New pages on established sites often get their first AI citation within days to a few weeks. Profound found a median of 6.81 days across about 900 pages, Xpand Media 18 days and LeadsNow 26 days. Steady brand visibility on buyer prompts usually takes about three months, and business impact three to six months.

How long does GEO take compared with AEO?

The work and the timelines overlap. Goodie, an AEO agency, estimates 2 to 4 weeks for technical answer-format wins (schema, FAQ formatting) on established domains, 8 to 16 weeks for consistent citations in longer AI answers, and 4 to 6 months for stable visibility across several engines. These are agency estimates, not controlled measurements.

How long does it take to get cited by ChatGPT?

In Semrush's test, ChatGPT search cited 8 of 81 new pages after one day and 34 by day 30, and cited pages kept their citations. Profound measured a median of 6.81 days to a first ChatGPT or Claude citation. Answers that come from ChatGPT's training data take much longer and often need a new model release.

How long does it take to appear in Google AI Overviews?

A page first has to be indexed and eligible for a snippet in Google Search, and Google says crawling can take from several days to several months. In Semrush's test, Google AI Mode cited 36% of new pages within 24 hours on a high-authority domain, but citations were volatile and fell by more than half from their peak by day 30.

Is Perplexity faster than ChatGPT for AEO?

Usually, yes. Perplexity searches the live web on almost every query, and Goodie reports citations within days on authoritative domains. In PromptCensus's 2026 data from Japan, ChatGPT barely cited new articles at all, but Perplexity took about twice as long as Gemini to cite them. Judge each engine on its own clock.

Why did my AI citations disappear?

Citation churn is normal. Passionfruit found 68% of queries that produced citations one month didn't produce them the next, and Trakkr found the median brand's citations halve within 31 days of a peak. Judge the trend across repeated checks over 8 to 12 weeks, not a single result.

When should I give up on AEO?

Don't give up at day 30; a flat start is normal. If a new page is crawlable and indexed but still uncited at day 60, rewrite it. If your appearance rate on a fixed prompt set hasn't moved at day 90, change the strategy, usually towards earning more third-party coverage, rather than publishing more of the same.

Who is the best AEO agency for realistic timelines?

Choose an agency that shows results per engine on a fixed prompt set, sets day-30, 60 and 90 checkpoints, and can earn press coverage, because that's what lasting citations depend on.
